name: CA-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Laura Friedman running with a large financial edge
Republican challenger raised under $60k with minimal cash
Markets price a Democratic win near certainty
model.rationale: This Los Angeles-area seat leans Democratic by about 21 points, and incumbent Laura Friedman holds a huge fundraising and cash-on-hand advantage over Scott Meyers, who has almost no money. With no contrary polling or ratings, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic win of roughly 25 points.
model.watch: A surprise influx of outside spending against Friedman or unusually low Democratic turnout in a low-profile general could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
CA-30 is a heavily Democratic Los Angeles-area district where first-term incumbent Laura Friedman advanced to the general election. The seat's partisan lean of about 21 points Democratic gives any Republican nominee a steep uphill climb, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive.

Friedman has raised roughly $828,000 and holds about $469,000 in cash, while Republican Scott Meyers has raised under $60,000 with only about $2,600 on hand and no outside support. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 95 percent. The forecast is a Safe Democratic hold with an expected margin near 25 points, though uncertainty is somewhat elevated because no district polls are available.
